subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Vehicle-to-Vehicle Communication
description: A quick, practical guide to Vehicle-to-Vehicle Communication.

hook.text: Your car can see a few hundred meters ahead, but it can't see around a building or a hill.

buildup.text: A hidden crash, black ice, or a red-light runner is invisible until it's too late.

discovery.text: V2V lets cars broadcast speed, position, and direction to every nearby vehicle at once.

twist.text: Your car could warn you about a crash around the corner before you can even see it.

climax.text: A massive US pilot in Ann Arbor showed V2V could prevent up to 80 percent of crashes.

punchline.text: Cars that talk to each other crash far less often.

quiz.question: What does V2V communication allow cars to share?

details.summary: Vehicle-to-vehicle communication lets cars exchange data about speed, position, and braking through short-range radio, enabling warnings about hidden dangers long before a driver could see them.
details.whyItMatters: V2V technology could prevent up to 80 percent of non-impaired crashes by alerting drivers to dangers beyond their line of sight, such as a car braking hard around a blind curve ahead.
takeaways: Cars broadcast position and speed data several times per second
Drivers receive alerts about hidden hazards ahead in real time
V2V could prevent millions of crashes annually when widespread

faq.question: What technology does vehicle-to-vehicle communication use?
faq.answer: V2V primarily uses dedicated short-range communications radio or cellular vehicle-to-everything technology to transmit basic safety messages including position, speed, heading, and brake status.

faq.question: When will most cars have vehicle-to-vehicle communication?
faq.answer: Adoption has been slow due to regulatory delays and the need for critical mass. Some manufacturers have begun including the hardware, but widespread deployment likely requires government mandates.
